name: Donner-Houghton House (156 E St. John St)
shape_note: Two-storey Victorian (Tasha Donner / Sherman O. Houghton), NRHP 2002; vacant, destroyed by a four-alarm fire 19 Jul 2007 and demolished for safety (removed from the NRHP 2013). start_year = HRI ESTIMATEDYR c1881 (ESTIMATE); end_year 2007 from the fire report (demolition late 2007, month not verified). HRI IDNUMBER 904 (its TRUEYR field says 2017: the HRI year field of demolished resources is NOT the demolition year). Position = HRI point. 1915: outside traced coverage; 1950: outside traced coverage.

name: San Jose City Hall in the plaza (Market Plaza / City Park)
shape_note: City hall in the middle of the plaza (now Plaza de Cesar Chavez), 1887-1958 per Metro Silicon Valley 1997 ('Old City Hall'), demolished 1958 after the city moved to the new civic centre on N. First St. Footprint traced from the 1915 Sanborn sheet 90 (id 004_0090_b16, brick, 972 m2; 1950 sheet: 008_0090_b50) - prefer the traced geometry; height not found. start_year: construction 1887-1889 (ESTIMATE 1887 as given by the source).

name: Hotel Montgomery at its original site (S. First St at San Antonio St)
shape_note: William Binder's 1911 hotel was moved 57 m (187 ft) south on 29 Jan 2000 to 211 S. First St, where it stands (reopened 2004): this row is the building at its first site only (1911-2000). Footprint traced from the 1915 Sanborn sheet 90 (004_0090_f56, 2,198 m2 incl. the wing; 1950: 008_0090_x84). Storeys 4 = ESTIMATE from photos (not read off the sheet).

name: Naval Hospital Oakland (Oak Knoll): main hospital building
shape_note: Oak Knoll Naval Hospital opened 1942 in temporary wards; ground broken 7 Dec 1965 for the permanent 597-bed hospital, completed mid-1968; base closed 1996; the 11-storey main building was imploded 8 Apr 2011. Position = the article's coordinate (three decimals, about +/-100 m: LOW CONFIDENCE); footprint 90x25 m and height (11 x 3.9 m) are ESTIMATES. The wartime wards around it are not drawn.

name: Hotel Vendome (549 N. First St, San Jose)
shape_note: Queen Anne resort hotel of 150 rooms in 11 acres of grounds (Jacob Lenzen & Son, 1888-89; annex wing 1903), closed 30 Apr 1930 and demolished; the grounds were subdivided (houses of the 1930s-50s stand there today). Position = the article's coordinate; footprint 75x18 m and 3 storeys are ESTIMATES from photographs (main block only, towers and the annex not drawn).

name: J. Henry Meyer Memorial Library (Stanford)
shape_note: Undergraduate library by John Carl Warnecke, dedicated 2 Dec 1966, closed 22 Aug 2014 and demolished Feb-Mar 2015 (now Meyer Green). Position = the article's coordinate; footprint 60x60 m, 4 storeys and height are ESTIMATES (square pavilion with a deep colonnade).

name: Warren Hall (Cal State East Bay, Hayward)
shape_note: 13-storey administration tower of the Hayward campus, built 1969-71, seen from across the bay; seismically unsafe (Hayward fault), imploded 17 Aug 2013. Position = the article's coordinate; footprint 30x30 m and height (13 x 3.9 m) are ESTIMATES.

name: Cowell Memorial Hospital (UC Berkeley)
shape_note: Student hospital by Arthur Brown Jr. (entrance and south wing 1930, later additions), NRHP-listed 6 Jan 1993 and demolished the same year for the Haas School of Business (1995, today's footprints). Position = the article's coordinate; footprint 50x30 m and 4 storeys are ESTIMATES.

name: Key Route Inn (Broadway at Grand Ave, Oakland)
shape_note: Half-timbered hotel of the Key System, opened 7 May 1907 on the west side of Broadway straddling what is now West Grand Avenue (the Key trains ran through the building); badly burned 8 Sep 1930, reopened Dec 1930, torn down April-May 1932 so that Grand Avenue could be cut through - the site is roadway today. Position and footprint area (4,469 m2, incl. the train arcade) = the outline drawn on the Oakland LocalWiki map (localwiki.org/oakland/Key_Route_Inn; not a survey); 4 storeys is an ESTIMATE from photographs. Inside the 1912 Sanborn coverage of downtown Oakland: prefer the traced outline if one exists.

name: Chevrolet (GM) Oakland Assembly plant (73rd Ave at MacArthur Blvd)
shape_note: The auto industry's first West Coast assembly plant, opened by Chevrolet in 1916; replaced by Fremont Assembly in the summer of 1963 (end_year = closure; the demolition year before Eastmont Mall, now Eastmont Town Center, was built on the site is not verified). Position = the article's coordinate; footprint 250x120 m and 2 storeys are ESTIMATES (the plant was enlarged several times; one block drawn).

name: Saint Mary's College, the 'Brickpile' (Broadway at 30th St, Oakland)
shape_note: Saint Mary's College moved from San Francisco to Oakland in 1889; its brick main building at 30th St and Broadway (the 'Brickpile') was badly damaged by fire and the college left for Moraga in 1928 (end_year = the move; demolition year not verified). California Historical Landmark 676 marks the site at 3093 Broadway: position = that address (geocoded, +/-40 m). Footprint 60x25 m and 5 storeys are ESTIMATES from photographs.

name: Tubbs Hotel (East 12th St between 4th and 5th Avenues, Oakland)
shape_note: 200-room resort hotel of Hiram Tubbs in the town of Brooklyn, opened 1871 on 'an entire 300-foot block' of Washington St (East 12th St from 1872) between today's 4th and 5th Avenues, in landscaped grounds; burned 14 Aug 1893 and the ruin was razed. Position = centre of the block outlined on the Oakland LocalWiki map; footprint 70x40 m and 3 storeys are ESTIMATES from the Taber photographs.

name: Montgomery Ward & Co. store and mail-order warehouse (2825 E. 14th St, Oakland)
shape_note: Oakland's largest industrial building (W. H. McCaully, 1923): nine-storey concrete, five connected structures on a 10-acre site at 2825 East 14th St (International Blvd), Fruitvale - retail store below, West Coast mail-order warehouse above. Empty for 11 years, demolished 2000 after a preservation lawsuit; the Cesar E. Chavez Education Center (2003) stands on the site. Position = centre of the complex outlined on the Oakland LocalWiki map (230x133 m incl. yards); footprint 150x70 m is an ESTIMATE of the main block.

name: Oak Hall, Arbor Villa (F. M. 'Borax' Smith estate, Oakland)
shape_note: Three-storey mansion of at least 42 rooms built 1893-95 for Francis Marion 'Borax' Smith (Walter J. Mathews) in the Arbor Villa estate off Park Boulevard; contents auctioned 1930, land from 1931, house torn down 13 Jan 1932 (the estate's palm trees remain). Position = the marker on the Oakland LocalWiki map inside the estate outline (not checked against the 1912 Sanborn sheet: LOW CONFIDENCE, +/-60 m); footprint 35x25 m is an ESTIMATE. The estate's water tower, stables and guest houses are not drawn.

name: Berkeley Inn (2501 Haste St at Telegraph Ave, Berkeley)
shape_note: Hotel by Joseph Cather Newsom, built 1911 on the north-east corner of Haste St and Telegraph Ave; City of Berkeley Landmark 9 Nov 1987; destroyed by fire and demolished in 1990 - the lot stood empty for more than thirty years. Position = the article's coordinate; footprint 30x25 m, 4 storeys and brick are ESTIMATES. Inside the 1911 Sanborn coverage of the Southside.

name: Hacienda del Pozo de Verona (Phoebe Hearst estate, Pleasanton)
shape_note: Phoebe Apperson Hearst's country house, built 1894-98 (A. C. Schweinfurth; large additions by Julia Morgan), the Castlewood Country Club's home from 1924; burned down in 1969 (the club's present clubhouse postdates the fire). Position = the article's coordinate; footprint 70x35 m and 2 storeys are ESTIMATES (towers and courtyards not drawn).

name: California State Normal School, 1881 building (Washington Square, San Jose)
shape_note: Second Normal School building on Washington Square (the first, 1872, burned 10 Feb 1880), opened 1881; declared unsafe after the 18 April 1906 earthquake and torn down; Tower Hall (1910) and its quadrangle replaced it. Position = the Tower Hall quadrangle in the middle of the square (ESTIMATE, +/-40 m: LOW CONFIDENCE); footprint 80x40 m and 3 storeys are ESTIMATES from photographs.

name: Circle Star Theater (2 Circle Star Way, San Carlos)
shape_note: Theatre in the round with a revolving stage, opened 1964 (ground broken 9 Mar 1964), closed December 1993; a fire on 18 Apr 1997 damaged the backstage and the building was then demolished for the Circle Star Center offices (end_year 1997: month not verified). Position = the article's coordinate; the round hall is drawn as a 60x60 m block 12 m high - ESTIMATES.

name: Jackling House (Woodside)
shape_note: Spanish Colonial Revival mansion by George Washington Smith for copper magnate Daniel C. Jackling, 1925 (17,250 sq ft / 1,603 m2 of floor space); owned by Steve Jobs from 1984 and demolished in February 2011 after a long preservation suit. Position = the article's coordinate; footprint 45x22 m and 2 storeys are ESTIMATES.

name: Tavern of Tamalpais (East Peak, Mount Tamalpais)
shape_note: Summit hotel and restaurant at the upper terminus of the Mill Valley & Mt. Tamalpais Scenic Railway, opened 1896; a kitchen fire in 1923 destroyed most of it. Position = the East Peak terminus flat (today's parking / picnic area; ESTIMATE, +/-50 m: LOW CONFIDENCE); footprint 40x15 m and 2 storeys are ESTIMATES from photographs (verandas and dance pavilion not drawn).

name: Tavern of Tamalpais, rebuilt (East Peak, Mount Tamalpais)
shape_note: Smaller one-storey tavern without overnight rooms (Bliss & Faville) built after the 1923 fire; the railway closed in 1930; the tavern closed after a New Year's dance in 1949 and was razed by the Marin Municipal Water District in 1950 (Marin History Museum; other accounts say 'in the 1950s' after a windstorm took the roof). Position as the 1896 tavern (ESTIMATE, +/-50 m); footprint 30x15 m is an ESTIMATE.

name: Sonoma County Courthouse of 1884 (Courthouse Square, Santa Rosa)
shape_note: First purpose-built county courthouse, opened 1884 on the plaza (Old Courthouse Square) and ruined by the earthquake of 18 April 1906 (PCAD 25585). Position = the middle of the square, which holds no building today. Footprint, storeys and material are ESTIMATES from photographs (domed two-storey masonry building).

name: Sonoma County Courthouse of 1909 (Courthouse Square, Santa Rosa)
shape_note: Second courthouse on the square, erected 1908-09 after the earthquake, opened 1909 and in use until 1966, then demolished (PCAD 25584: "erected in 1908-1909, and this functioned here until 1966"). Position = the middle of Old Courthouse Square. Footprint, storeys and facing material are ESTIMATES from photographs.

name: Santa Rosa Free Public Library (Carnegie library, E St at Fourth St)
shape_note: Carnegie library dedicated March 1904, badly damaged in 1906 and rebuilt; condemned as unsafe in 1960 and demolished in 1964 (Wikipedia list of Carnegie libraries; Sonoma County Library article). The Central Library of 1967 replaced it on the same block: position to the block (E Street at Fourth), LOW confidence on the exact spot. Footprint, storeys and material are ESTIMATES.

name: Santa Cruz Carnegie (Main) Library (224 Church St)
shape_note: W. H. Weeks, Richardsonian Romanesque; opened 28 April 1904, demolished in 1966 to make way for the present Downtown Branch on the same site (Santa Cruz Public Libraries local history: "The first Santa Cruz Carnegie Library (1904-1966)"). Position = today's library at 224 Church St. Footprint, storeys and material are ESTIMATES.

name: Casa del Rey Hotel (Beach St at Cliff St, Santa Cruz)
shape_note: Mission Revival resort hotel built 1911 by Fred Swanton across Beach Street from the Casino; seriously damaged by the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake and demolished (Wikipedia; coordinates from the article). The site is the Boardwalk car park. Footprint, height and storeys are ESTIMATES.

name: Hotel Metropole (1111 Pacific Ave, Santa Cruz)
shape_note: Italianate commercial hotel built 1908 (Charles Kay), NRHP 1979; demolished after severe damage in the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake (Wikipedia; coordinates from the article). Footprint ESTIMATE. The replacement building on the site has no recorded year in the map data.

name: Cooper House (Santa Cruz County Courthouse of 1894-95, Pacific Ave at Cooper St)
shape_note: Courthouse by Comstock and Beck built 1894-95 after the fire of 1894; county offices left in the 1960s and it reopened in 1969 as the Cooper House shops and restaurants; damaged by the 1989 Loma Prieta earthquake and demolished that year (Santa Cruz LocalWiki: "The Original Cooper House 1894-1989"). Position = 110 Cooper St, where the 1999 Cooper House stands. Footprint and storeys are ESTIMATES.

name: St. George Hotel (Pacific Ave, Santa Cruz)
shape_note: Santa Cruz LocalWiki: the St. George Hotel "rose out of the ashes of an 1894 fire, then perished in a 1990 fire" (damaged in the 1989 earthquake). start_year 1895 = ESTIMATE (rebuilt after the fire of April 1894). Position = today's Hotel St. George building (roll year 1993) on the same site. Footprint and storeys are ESTIMATES.

name: Neptune Casino (first Boardwalk casino, Santa Cruz)
shape_note: Fred Swanton's first casino, built 1904 (opened 14 June 1904), burned down completely on 22 June 1906 (Santa Cruz LocalWiki; Wikipedia, Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk). Position = the present Casino / Cocoanut Grove of 1907, built on its site. Footprint and storeys are ESTIMATES.

name: Sea Beach Hotel (Beach Hill, Santa Cruz)
shape_note: Queen Anne resort hotel above Main Beach: grew out of the Ocean View House of the 1870s and opened as the Sea Beach Hotel in 1890; burned to the ground on 12 June 1912 (Santa Cruz Sentinel, C. Swift, 2 July 2000, in the Santa Cruz Public Libraries local history index). Position = the site of today's Casablanca Inn (Beach St at Main St), to about 50 m. Footprint and storeys are ESTIMATES.

name: Big Basin Redwoods State Park headquarters (administration building)
shape_note: Log-and-timber administration building built by the Civilian Conservation Corps in 1936; destroyed by the CZU Lightning Complex fire in August 2020 (Wikipedia). Position = the park headquarters coordinates of the article, to about 50 m. Footprint ESTIMATE.

name: Byron Hot Springs, first hotel
shape_note: Three-storey wooden hotel built 1889 by Lewis Mead; destroyed by fire on 25 July 1901 (Wikipedia). Position = the resort's hotel site, where the third hotel of 1914 stands; exact footprint not known (ESTIMATE).

name: Byron Hot Springs, second hotel
shape_note: Three-storey Moorish-style stucco hotel built 1901-02; burned in 1912 (Wikipedia). Position = the resort's hotel site, where the third hotel of 1914 stands; exact footprint not known (ESTIMATE).

name: Napa County Courthouse of 1856
shape_note: The original county courthouse of 1856, replaced on the same plaza by the present courthouse of 1878 (Wikipedia, Napa County Courthouse Plaza). Position = the courthouse plaza; footprint, storeys and material unknown (ESTIMATES).
